title: A Novel Surgical Technique As a Foundation for In Vivo Partial Liver Engineering in Rat
protocol: Place the rat in an induction chamber and anesthetize the rat with 4% vaporized isoflurane and 100% oxygen at 0.5 L/min for about 3 min, until the rat is completely anesthetized.
Take the rat out of the induction chamber and measure its body weight.
Shave the fur of the surgical region on the abdomen.
Place the animal back into the isoflurane chamber for an additional 2 min to deepen anesthesia.
Place the rat on the operation table in supine position.
Fix the anesthesia mask to the mouth region of the rat and keep the animal anesthetized with a continuous gas flow of 2% vaporized isoflurane and 100% oxygen at a flow rate of 0.5 L/min.
Fix the limbs with pieces of tape.
Apply vet ointment on both eyes to prevent dryness.
Administer buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg subcutaneously, to relieve pain during the operation period.
Disinfect the surgical field of the abdomen with 3 rounds of iodine tincture followed by 2 rounds of 70% alcohol.
Place sterilized gauze around the area where the incision will be made to only leave the operation field of the abdomen exposed.
Proceed to perform the operation when the toe-pinch withdrawal reflex of the rat is absent.
Make a transverse abdominal skin and muscle incision using scissors and an electrical coagulator.
Fix and pull the xiphoid process toward the head using a 4-0 polypropylene suture.
Open the peritoneal cavity by pulling both sides of the abdominal walls towards the head with two subcostal hooks to expose the liver.
Cover the duodenum and small intestine in the abdominal cavity with a moistened gauze to avoid drying.
Lift left and right median lobes up using a moistened gauze and hold them against the thorax to better expose the hilum of the liver.
Place the rat under a stereomicroscope at 8X magnification.
Drop some warm saline into the abdomen and onto the surface of the liver and intestines every several minutes to prevent drying during the procedure.
Dissect the left portal vein and ligate it with a 6-0 silk suture at the base.

Block the left hepatic artery, the left bile duct along with the left median portal vein, the left median hepatic artery, and the left median bile duct with micro clamps to prevent flow of the perfusate to the left median lobe.
Separate the left lateral lobe by cutting off the surrounding ligaments of the lobe with micro scissors.
Block the left lateral hepatic vein by clamping at the base of the left lateral lobe with micro clamps.
Make an incision in the front wall of the left portal vein using a 24-G needle-dwelling catheter.
Withdraw the catheter and take the needle out to obtain a needle-free 24-G catheter.
Connect the needle-free catheter to a perfusion tube, which is connected to a 20-mL syringe containing 15 mL of 40 U/mL heparinized saline on a perfusion pump.
Turn on the perfusion pump to expel air from the tube and the catheter.
Turn off the perfusion pump.
Insert the needle-free catheter into the left portal vein via the punctured incision.
Make another incision at the margin of the exposed region of the left lateral hepatic vein using a 22- or 24-G needle-dwelling catheter.
Remove the catheter and take out the needle to create a needle-free 22-G catheter.
Turn on the perfusion pump to perfuse heparinized saline into the left lateral lobe via the 24-G cannulated needle-free catheter of the left portal vein at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Absorb out-flowing waste fluid around the incision area using dry gauze.
Cannulate the left lateral hepatic vein via the punctured incision with the 22-G needle-free catheter to generate a fluid outlet.
Perfuse the left lateral lobe with heparinized saline for approximately 20 minutes, followed by only saline for 2 hours, 3 hours, or 4 hours as required.
Turn off the pump to stop perfusion.
Take off both catheters from the left portal vein and the left lateral hepatic vein.
Close the incision of the left portal vein with an 11-0 polyamide suture.
Close the incision of the left lateral hepatic vein with an 11-0 polyamide suture.
Unclamp the left lateral hepatic vein.
Unclamp the left median portal vein, left bile duct, and left hepatic artery.
Cut off the ligature on the left portal vein to reopen the vein.
Close the muscle layer of the abdominal wall by interrupted suturing with a 4-0 absorbable polyglactin 910 suture.
Close the skin layer of the abdominal wall by interrupted suturing with a 4-0 absorbable polydioxanone suture.
Disinfect the skin incision with 70% alcohol.
Place the animal on a warming pad for resuscitation for about 10 min.
Put the animal into a new cage.
Administer buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg subcutaneously 2x a day for a consecutive 3 d postoperatively to release pain.
